Each review is tied to a specific product purchase through the order_item_id, ensuring eligibility for review submission only after delivery. Reviews include a numeric rating (1-5 stars) and optional text feedback from customers. A review may be edited by the customer after creation, with changes tracked via snapshots in the shopping_mall_review_snapshots table.

Reviews remain visible to customers and sellers even after deletion (is_deleted = true), preserving their contribution to overall product ratings while removing them from public display. Administrative deletion removes the review from rating calculation entirely.

This entity forms the core of the product review system, enabling peer-to-peer feedback that influences purchase decisions across the shopping mall platform.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who wrote this review. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: The product being reviewed. {@link shopping_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: The specific order item this review is based on. Required to verify purchase completion before reviewing. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: parent_review_id
foreignFields.description: For reply reviews (nested comments), this references the parent review being replied to. A null value indicates a top-level review. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Numeric rating from 1 to 5 stars. Required field that drives product average rating calculation. Only non-deleted reviews are included in average calculation.

plainFields.name: text
plainFields.description: Optional text content describing the customer's experience with the product. May be null, empty, or contain detailed feedback.

plainFields.name: is_deleted
plainFields.description: Marks whether the review has been deleted by the customer or admin. When true, the review is hidden from public display but remains in the system for rating calculation and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was deleted. Will be null if the review is active. Required for determining visibility and audit history.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was first created. Immutable field that records the initial submission time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was last edited. Updated with each modification by the customer.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots capturing the state of reviews at time of creation, edit, or deletion, preserving before/after values and actor information.

Each snapshot records the complete state of a review at the moment of change, providing an audit trail for dispute resolution, compliance, and historical analysis. The system preserves every modification to a review - whether initiated by the customer, the seller, or an administrator - to ensure transparency and accountability in the review ecosystem.

Snapshots are the foundation of review integrity: they prevent tampering, provide verifiable evidence of change history, and ensure that even deleted reviews remain accessible for audit purposes. Each snapshot contains every field that was modified, including rating, text content, and deletion status, along with the identity of the actor who made the change and the precise timestamp.

The data in these snapshots is used by customers to view their own review history, by sellers to understand how their product's reviews have evolved, and by administrators to investigate complaints or policy violations. Critically, no snapshot can be modified or deleted once created, ensuring complete integrity of the historical record.

Snapshots are referenced by the parent shopping_mall_reviews record through review_id, and every snapshot contains both the previous and current state of the review, enabling complete reconstruction of its entire lifecycle from creation to final state.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: The parent review record being snapshotted. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who made the review change, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: The seller who responded to a review action, if applicable. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who performed moderation actions on the review. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: The numerical star rating (1-5) of the review at the time of this snapshot. Always required.

plainFields.name: text
plainFields.description: The full text content of the review at the time of this snapshot. Will be null if text was cleared during edit or deletion.

plainFields.name: is_deleted
plainFields.description: Whether the review was marked as deleted at the time of this snapshot. False indicates active review, true indicates it has been deleted by customer or admin.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The precise timestamp (UTC) when this snapshot was created, recording when the change occurred.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: The type of actor that triggered this snapshot: 'customer' (review created/edited/deleted by customer), 'admin' (review deleted or hidden by administrator), or 'system' (automatic changes like auto-delivery).

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Sequential integer representing the revision number of this snapshot, starting at 1 for the initial review creation. Each edit or deletion increments by 1 to maintain chronological order.

plainFields.name: previous_rating
plainFields.description: The previous rating value before this snapshot took effect, for edit operations. Null when creating new review or if action is deletion.

plainFields.name: previous_text
plainFields.description: The previous text content before this snapshot took effect, for edit operations. Null when creating new review or if action is deletion.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: If the review was deleted in this snapshot, records the exact timestamp of deletion. Null for active or edited reviews.

plainFields.name: admin_reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by an administrator for deleting or hiding the review. Requires at least 10 characters when actor_type is 'admin'. Null for customer-initiated actions.

plainFields.name: deleted_by_system
plainFields.description: True if this deletion was triggered automatically by system rules (e.g., no action taken for 30 days). False if triggered by user or admin.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_votes
models.description:
Tracks up/down votes from customers on reviews to identify helpful content.

This table enables community moderation by allowing customers to indicate whether a review was helpful. Each customer can cast exactly one vote per review, with the vote type indicating up (helpful) or down (not helpful). The voting system helps surface high-quality reviews to the top of content lists and provides feedback to reviewers.

Votes are immutable after creation (no updates) but can be deleted if a customer wishes to remove their vote. This table does not store the content of the review itself but links directly to the review being voted on via foreign key.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: The review being voted on. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who cast this vote. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: vote_type
plainFields.description: Type of vote: 'up' for helpful, 'down' for not helpful. Must always be one of these two values.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the vote was cast. Always set during creation, immutable.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this record. Only updated when the vote is deleted (set to null).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the vote was deleted by the customer (soft delete). If null, vote is active.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_reports
models.description:
Reports of reviews for policy violations, including reporter identity, reason for report, and status for administrative review.

This table captures user-initiated reports of reviews that violate platform policies (e.g., profanity, spam, false information). Each report is initiated by a customer, seller, or administrator and requires administrative action to resolve. The system preserves a complete audit trail of report creation, status changes, and resolution, aligning with the platform's snapshot principle for all business-critical modifications.

Reports are linked to both the user who submitted them (reporter) and the review being reported. Administrators have full authority to review reports and take appropriate actions, including hiding reviews from public view or taking action against abusive reporters. Reports cannot be modified once created, but their status evolves through the workflow from pending → approved → rejected.

This entity follows the primary stance because administrators need independent API access to list all reports, filter by status, search report reasons, and update multiple reports in bulk without needing to navigate through individual review details. The report itself is an administrative work item with its own lifecycle, separate from the review it concerns.

foreignFields.name: reporter_id
foreignFields.description: The user who submitted this review report. This references the user_id in the Actors component's customer table. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: The specific review being reported. This references the review_id in the Reviews component's shopping_mall_reviews table. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the reporter for this review report. Can include text explaining why the review violates platform policy. Supports full-text search for administrative review.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of this report. Valid values are: pending (initial state), approved (verdict: report valid - review should be hidden), rejected (verdict: report invalid - review remains visible). Status transitions are immutable after administrative action.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this report was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this report's status was last updated by an administrator.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this report was logically deleted (soft delete). A report remains visible in audit logs but is hidden from active management interfaces if deleted.

models.name: shopping_mall_cancellation_requests
models.description:
Customer requests to cancel order items before shipment, containing request reason, status (pending/approved/rejected), timestamps, and actor references.

Stores cancellation requests initiated by customers for order items with status "paid". Each request includes a reason for cancellation and tracks the status of the request (pending, approved, or rejected). The request is linked to a specific order item and records when it was created, when a response was given, and by which actor (seller or administrator). This table enables audit trails, approval workflows, and inventory restoration upon approval.

The cancellation request lifecycle involves:
- Customer submits request with reason
- Seller or administrator reviews and responds
- Status transitions trigger snapshot creation
- If approved, inventory is restored via inventory_records
- If rejected, request remains closed

All data is preserved for compliance and dispute resolution purposes.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: The order item being canceled. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: responded_by
foreignFields.description: The actor (seller) who responded to the request. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the customer for requesting cancellation. Must be a non-empty text field.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the cancellation request. Valid values are: pending, approved, rejected. Default is 'pending'.

plainFields.name: requested_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer submitted the cancellation request.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when a seller or administrator responded to the request. Null until response is given.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the record was created. Always equals requested_at at creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the record was last updated (e.g., status change).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null while active. Set when request is purged or archived.

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_requests
models.description:
Stores requests from customers to refund delivered order items, containing request reason, status (pending/approved/rejected), timestamps, and actor references.

Each refund request is initiated by a customer after their order item has been marked as delivered. Customers provide a reason for the refund, and sellers can approve or reject the request. Every status change must be recorded in the corresponding snapshot table, preserving an immutable audit trail.

The refund request record does not store inventory changes — those are handled separately in the Inventory component. This table only captures the request lifecycle, response, and status transition. Refund requests cannot be created until the associated order item has been delivered, and must be responded to within the platform's policy window.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: The order item for which this refund is requested. {@link shopping_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: The customer who initiated this refund request. {@link shopping_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: responded_by
foreignFields.description: The actor (seller) who responded to this refund request. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the customer for requesting a refund to the seller. Typically includes product dissatisfaction, delivery issues, or incorrect items.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the refund request. Must be one of: pending, approved, rejected. State transitions are controlled by business logic and require a corresponding snapshot entry.

plainFields.name: requested_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund request was initially submitted by the customer. Always precedes any response timestamp.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when a seller or admin responded to the refund request (approved or rejected). Only set once request is responded to.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp for audit purposes. Never modified after initial creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this refund request record. Updated whenever status or response fields change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-delete timestamp. If set, the refund request is considered logically deleted but remains in the database for audit purposes.

models.name: shopping_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots capturing cancellation request state (reason, status, responder, timestamp) at each modification.

Preserves the exact state of cancellation requests for audit trail and dispute resolution purposes.

When a cancellation request's status changes from pending to approved or rejected, a snapshot is created
that captures the request's state at that moment, including the reason text, the final status, the timestamp
when the response was made, and the user who made the response.

This snapshot is immutable and cannot be altered after creation, providing a legally valid record
of the cancellation handling process.

These snapshots are referenced when resolving disputes about whether a cancellation was properly
processed, approved, or rejected by a seller.

The is_deleted field and deleted_at field allow for the permanent removal of data while preserving
history - a snapshot can be marked as deleted without eliminating its record from the audit trail.

foreignFields.name: cancellation_request_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the cancellation_request being snapshotted. {@link shopping_mall_cancellation_requests.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the customer for requesting cancellation.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The status of the cancellation request at the time of snapshot. Valid values: pending, approved, rejected.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller responded to the cancellation request. This is the snapshot creation time.

plainFields.name: responded_by
plainFields.description: The user ID of the seller who responded to the cancellation request.

plainFields.name: is_deleted
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this snapshot record itself has been logically deleted (not applicable to the original cancellation request).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When the snapshot was marked as deleted. NULL means not deleted.

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_request_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots capturing refund request state at each modification.

This table preserves the complete state of refund requests including reason, status, timestamp, and responder information at the moment each change occurred. These snapshots serve as an audit trail for financial and customer service compliance purposes.

Each snapshot is immutable and represents a point-in-time state of a refund_request. When a refund request's status changes from pending to approved or rejected, a new snapshot is created to preserve both the previous state and the updated state. This ensures complete traceability for dispute resolution and regulatory compliance.

The table links to the main refund_request record through refund_request_id and captures the business decision maker (responded_by) along with the exact time of response (responded_at). This allows administrators and customers to audit the entire history of refund processing.

foreignFields.name: refund_request_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the main refund_request being snapshot. {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the customer for requesting the refund.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The state of the refund request at the time of this snapshot. Valid values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: The exact timestamp when the seller or administrator responded to the refund request.

plainFields.name: responded_by
plainFields.description: The user ID of the seller or administrator who responded to this refund request. {@link shopping_mall_users.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this snapshot record was created in the database.

plainFields.name: is_deleted
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this snapshot was logically deleted in accordance with retention policies.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this snapshot was marked as deleted, if applicable.
